headline: Trump says he will hold off new Iran strikes 'for the time being' at the behest of Gulf neighbours
dek: US President Donald Trump said on Monday (Nov 9) he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the time being, after appeals from countries in the region, including from Qatar's prime minister in White House talks. He said he was acting 'at the behest of countries that are their…
sources: Reuters (via DZRH / GMA / Straits Times carries)
fault_line: Did the neighbours stop a war, or did Trump just pause it? - 'hold off for now' vs 'locked and loaded'.

sections.what_happened: US President Donald Trump said on Monday (Nov 9) he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the time being, after appeals from countries in the region, including from Qatar's prime minister in White House talks. He said he was acting 'at the behest of countries that are their neighbors' and specifically cited Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait. Trump also said he plans to keep up the naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now. Turkish President Erdogan said on Monday he told Trump Ankara did not want a new escalation. Iran's two-day truce proposal (end US blockade + lift some sanctions + halt bombing in return for Tehran ending its Hormuz blockade, then nuclear talks) remains rejected by Washington; Rubio calls Tehran's conditions 'outrageous and ridiculous'; Baghaei defends the plan as the most reasonable offer. Reuters also reports tanker attacks in the Gulf and Hormuz 'ramped up sharply in October and have continued at the highest rate since the start of the war' per international maritime agencies, and that Iran state TV claimed 11 tankers were 'disabled' over the past 10 days (claimant figure, NOT a counted figure).
sections.what_verified: Trump's own on-record words in a Reuters interview and a White House briefing-room appearance (Reuters T1, single family - the primary source itself). DZRH, GMA and Straits Times carries are the same Reuters family and add no family. The 11-tankers-disabled figure is Iran state TV (unregistered, no tier) and is NOT corroborated; Reuters' maritime-agency line (attacks at highest rate since war start) is a separate, wire-reported trend, not a count of disabled tankers.
sections.what_disputed: Rubio (Nov 8-9): 'I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough'; Tehran's conditions 'outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic'. UAE official Anwar Gargash (Nov 9): a comprehensive settlement 'appears difficult'; 'prepare for a long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted'. Israel still expects a strike eventually (Jerusalem Post, via secondary summary - unregistered). Trump himself keeps the option open: 'fully locked and loaded', blockade stays, no ceasefire guaranteed (0400-01).
sections.why_matters: The neighbours asked him to stop: Trump holds fire on Iran - but the blockade stays and no deal is near.
sections.context: Background: FOLLOW-UP to 0400-01 -- Trump says he will hold off new Iran strikes 'for the time being' at the behest of Gulf neighbours (Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait); blockade of Hormuz stays; no deal imminent

totw_analysis: Our read: The neighbours asked him to stop: Trump holds fire on Iran - but the blockade stays and no deal is near. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did the neighbours stop a war, or did Trump just pause it? - 'hold off for now' vs 'locked and loaded'.
